title: Hosted API: Embeddings + Rerank - Demo
summary: AE + SE demo of Hosted API embeddings + rerank for BrightFind search relevance use case. Walkthrough of embeddings endpoint, rerank endpoint, Console UI for monitoring, and Redwood Optimize recommendations. Discussed latency vs cost, SSO/KMS questions, pilot benchmarks and next steps: share pricing, security docs, and run a short benchmark with BrightFind sample queries.
action_items: Maya Chen: send pricing deck + hosted pilot terms by 2026-12-02
Arjun Patel: share sample benchmark script and minimal repro to run embeddings+rerank locally by 2026-12-04
Priya Menon (Customer): provide sample query set and dataset schema by 2026-12-03
next_steps: Security packet (SOC2/ISO docs) to be sent
Follow-up demo for dedicated latency tuning if pilot shows need
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-30
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Sara Lopez (BrightFind Head of Search), Tom Garcia (CTO), Priya Menon (ML Eng)

[00:00:05] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Maya, I'm the AE on this account, and with me is Arjun, our solutions engineer. Very excited to walk through Hosted API embeddings and the rerank flow that a lot of search teams use.

[00:00:20] Sara Lopez: Hey Maya, thanks. Quick context — we've been evaluating a replacement for our current Elastic-based rerank pipeline, we're seeing some drift in relevance and high infra cost. We're particularly interested in embeddings + rerank as a way to reduce retrieval failure and improve recency handling.

[00:00:40] Arjun Patel: Great. Quick question on stack — are you currently doing dense retrieval with FAISS or doing hybrid with BM25?

[00:00:50] Priya Menon: We're running a hybrid. BM25 for initial recall, then a small Faiss cluster for vectors. But scalability costs are rising and our ML infra team is stretched. We want something that drops in — low ops — but also predictable latency.

[00:01:10] Tom Garcia: Also SSO and KMS are table stakes for us. We can't move until we validate encryption at rest and audit logs.

[00:01:20] Maya Chen: Totally — we'll cover security and compliance at the end. Redwood's hosted API supports customer-managed KMS integrations and audit logs; we also have SOC2 and ISO docs we can share.

[00:01:35] Arjun Patel: Okay, demo plan: quick call flow: show embeddings endpoint, demonstrate vector generation and dimensionality, then rerank endpoint which takes candidate docs + query+embeds and returns a reorder with scores. I'll show the console for latency/cost breakdown and Optimize suggestions for batching/caching.

[00:02:05] Arjun Patel: (screen share) Here is a sample curl to /v1/embeddings. Notice payload: input is text array, model param, and you get back dense vectors. Example response — dimension 1536, floats. One note: model variants have different dimension sizes, we can pin to the variant you want.

[00:02:45] Priya Menon: Do you provide a canonical embedding recipe for semantic similarity and retention of chronology? We need to preserve recency signals.

[00:02:55] Arjun Patel: We recommend concatenating a small recency token in the prompt or using metadata in rerank scoring. But Optimize can propose a rerank blend where we combine dot-product on embeddings with a recency feature.

[00:03:20] Maya Chen: Also, you can do prefix caching — for highly repeated queries we can serve faster and cheaper.

[00:03:30] [00:03:50] Arjun Patel: Now showing rerank endpoint. You POST query, candidate documents with their embeddings or raw text; rerank returns reordered list with confidence scores and an explanation token. The response is JSON with score and reason. Quick demo with sample candidates — you can see initially Elastic baseline ranks slightly different, but rerank improves click-through in our internal benchmarks.

[00:04:20] Sara Lopez: When you say "explanation token", is that deterministic? We need to generate snippets for the UI showing why a doc was bumped up.

[00:04:30] Arjun Patel: It's a heuristic output from the model-based reranker — we surface top contributing features. Not a formal proof, but good for display. There may be occasional noise in language generation there, transcription note: sometimes the explanation text has small hallucinations, so we recommend validating with a lightweight rule filter.

[00:04:55] Tom Garcia: Latency — what are your P95 numbers for a typical embed+rerank call?

[00:05:05] Arjun Patel: Hosted defaults: embeddings are usually in the 30–120ms range depending on model and token length. Rerank depends on number of candidates — 10 candidates typically ~80–200ms P95. For strict SLOs we recommend our Dedicated offering but for many customers Hosted is fine.

[00:05:30] Priya Menon: And throughput? We'll run bursts of 200 qps during peak.

[00:05:40] Maya Chen: For that throughput, we'd suggest a pilot to measure real-world batching and cache hit rate. Optimize will give batching suggestions and model/quantization recommendations to reduce cost.

[00:06:00] [00:06:30] Arjun Patel: Console view: here's per-route token cost, per-request latency, and a trace view where you can see subcomponents: tokenization, serve time, rerank compute. You can also open a trace to see KV cache hits — sometimes transcribed as K-V cash — but that's the caching on prefix contexts.

[00:07:00] Priya Menon: Is there built-in A/B for rerank models? We want to test new ranking variants against control.

[00:07:10] Arjun Patel: Yes — rollouts support canary, weighted A/B, and automatic fallback if a variant breaches error or latency thresholds. We also tie regressions to a prompt set so you can alert on relevance drop.

[00:07:35] Sara Lopez: Security packet — can you confirm SSO/SAML and audit log retention length? We need at least 13 months of logs for audits.

[00:07:45] Maya Chen: We support SAML/SSO and can push audit logs to your SIEM via syslog or S3. Retention configurable; longer retention is an add-on. We'll include this in the security docs we send.

[00:08:05] Tom Garcia: About data residency — can we ensure embeddings never leave our region?

[00:08:15] Arjun Patel: For Hosted we host in multiple regions; you can pin to region. If policy requires stricter isolation, Private deployment is the option. We'll cover tradeoffs: Private gives full control but higher ops and contract terms.

[00:08:40] [00:09:05] Arjun Patel: Back to demo — example rerank payload: query text, candidates with ids and embeddings. You can also send only ids and we will fetch precomputed embeddings if you've uploaded an embedding catalog via the Console. That reduces token size in request.

[00:09:30] Priya Menon: How do we bulk upload precomputed embeddings?

[00:09:35] Arjun Patel: There's a bulk endpoint and Console import. We recommend chunked uploads and we handle storage + indexing. The system will return an id mapping and you can reference those ids in rerank requests.

[00:09:55] Sara Lopez: Any guidance on dimensionality and index size? We're currently at 1536 dims with 60M docs.

[00:10:05] Arjun Patel: For 60M, hosted storage is fine but cost matters — Optimize will recommend quantization profiles (8-bit/4-bit) and possibly sharding options. There's a tradeoff between vector precision and recall; we can share benchmark docs.

[00:10:30] [00:11:00] Maya Chen: Quick pause — Sara, is your timeline to have a pilot in the next 2–3 weeks?

[00:11:05] Sara Lopez: We want to start a pilot before holiday freeze — so yes, ASAP. We'll need pricing and security docs to sign off and maybe a small POC dataset.

[00:11:20] Maya Chen: Good — we'll send pricing and pilot terms. Arjun, on benchmarks you mentioned a small script?

[00:11:30] Arjun Patel: I'll share a minimal repro that'll run the embeddings+rerank loop and measure latency and tail percentiles. We'll also include a spreadsheet for you to drop in sample queries.

[00:11:45] Tom Garcia: One more nit — do you provide a way to pin model versions so outputs are stable for A/B evaluation?

[00:11:55] Arjun Patel: Yes, models are versioned and you can pin via the API or Console. Rollouts can also be used to shift traffic gradually.

[00:12:10] [00:12:40] Priya Menon: A question on cost: if we use precomputed embeddings and then only call rerank, how is billing handled? Is it per-embedding call or per-rerank call?

[00:12:50] Maya Chen: Billing separates embedding generation and rerank compute. If you use stored embeddings, you won't be billed for re-embedding that content, only for rerank compute tokens/units. We'll include an example cost model in the deck.

[00:13:10] Sara Lopez: Any hard limits on candidate counts? We typically send 50 candidates for freshness.

[00:13:20] Arjun Patel: Hosted supports up to 200 candidates but performance and cost scale. For 50 candidates expect higher latency; Optimize can suggest batching or a two-stage rerank (lightweight model then heavy rerank top K).

[00:13:45] [00:14:20] Arjun Patel: Now switching to Console Optimize tab — here's model recommendation: for your workload (short queries, 50 candidates), we recommend a quantized rerank variant and a medium-dimension embedding model. Also suggestions to increase cache TTL for recurring queries and apply prefix caching.

[00:14:40] Priya Menon: Can Optimize push configs or is it advisory?

[00:14:45] Arjun Patel: Mostly advisory by default. For Dedicated/private we can enable automated config application with guardrails. For Hosted it's opt-in to apply suggestions.

[00:15:05] Sara Lopez: Great. Any live examples of CTR improvements customers have seen?

[00:15:10] Maya Chen: We've seen 8–20% CTR uplift on average in e-commerce and knowledge base customers when switching from BM25+static heuristics to embeddings+rerank. Results vary by dataset.

[00:15:30] [00:16:00] Tom Garcia: Let's talk slas — if we do a Hosted pilot and then need guaranteed latency, what's the pathway?

[00:16:10] Maya Chen: If you need guaranteed latency, we typically transition to Dedicated with reserved capacity and SLA-backed P95 targets. We'll use pilot metrics to size Dedicated pools.

[00:16:35] Priya Menon: Any gotchas for GDPR/data deletion requests?

[00:16:40] Arjun Patel: We support deletion APIs and data residency options. For embeddings stored we can delete per-id. We'll include deletion policy in the security packet.

[00:17:05] [00:17:40] Sara Lopez: Ok let's recap next steps — we'll send sample dataset, Redwood will run a short pilot and share pricing and security docs, and Arjun will send the benchmark script.

[00:17:55] Maya Chen: Correct. We'll target onboarding the pilot next week, pending signatures. Anything else from your side?

[00:18:05] Tom Garcia: No, that covers it. Thanks.

[00:18:15] Maya Chen: Great thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the items we listed.

[00:18:25] (call wrap, small chitchat, meeting ends)

Notes: transcript contains occasional ASR errors (e.g., K-V cash instead of KV cache), some overlapping talk labeled as generic. Action items captured in metadata.
